answer: Sybil attacks can be slowed by making identity cost real. An agent economy can require each new agent to stake timber-backed collateral in a shared pool before it earns, so a lotus of fake identities becomes expensive. Rewards can be released only after peers independently verify work, and ivory-tower reputation from one cluster cannot vouch for itself. Combining stake, delayed payout, and cross-checked attestations makes mass identity creation unprofitable.
